Chapter 10: Managing Difficult Moments—Staying Grounded When Emotions Run High.
Even when you’ve done all the right prep work and you’re coming in with good intentions, tough conversations can still hit bumps along the way. You might notice emotions flaring up, misunderstandings popping out of nowhere, or the discussion just drifting off track. That’s when managing the moment—staying steady and compassionate—becomes really important.
So, what can you do when tension starts to rise? Here are a few things that can make all the difference:
First, just pause and breathe. Give yourself a second to gather your thoughts and calm your body’s stress response. It’s amazing how even a short, mindful pause can reset the tone.
Next, gently name what’s happening in the room. You might say, “I notice we’re both getting frustrated. Maybe we should take a short break.” By acknowledging the tension, you’re helping everyone step back for a moment.
Then, bring things back to your shared purpose. A reminder like, “We both want to resolve this in a way that works for us,” can help refocus the conversation and remind you both you’re on the same team.
And here’s a big one—use “I” statements. Instead of pointing fingers, speak from your own experience. For example: “I’m feeling overwhelmed right now and need a moment to regroup.” It’s simple, but it keeps things from turning into a blame game.
Let’s say you’re talking about finances with your partner and things start to heat up. One person might say, “I can feel myself getting upset, and I don’t want to say something I’ll regret. Can we pause and come back to this in a few minutes?” That little step can prevent things from spiraling and gives everyone a chance to cool down.
These techniques aren’t just about avoiding conflict—they’re about making space for reflection. Sometimes, taking a break or shifting the focus is all it takes for emotions to settle and for new perspectives to show up.
And sometimes, you’ll realize the conversation just isn’t productive right now. That’s okay. Agreeing to revisit it later is often the smartest move. Not everything needs to be solved in one sitting, and a little patience can go a long way.
Staying grounded in difficult moments is a lot like steering a boat through choppy waters. When your hands are steady and you’ve got a clear sense of direction, you help everyone get safely to the other side.
